html:
The Yamasee were a confederation of Native peoples formed in the 1600s from survivors of chiefdoms of Georgia broken by Spanish and English colonisation and disease. First noted by the Spanish in 1663, they lived near the coast from northern Florida to South Carolina, at times in Spanish missions in Guale.

In the 1680s many moved north into Carolina and became close trading partners and slave-raiding allies of the English, joining attacks on the missions of Spanish Florida, among them those of the Apalachee. Abuse by traders and mounting debts led them to rise in the Yamasee War of 1715, which nearly destroyed the colony. Defeated, most fled back to Spanish Florida near St. Augustine. Their survivors later merged into the Seminole and the Creek.
